proposed_branch: Instantiate and refine the polar R3m (No. 160) realization in the same R-centered hexagonal cell, starting from Hg z=0, Ni z=0.49340, and independent S sites z=0.11128 and 0.89015, then compare it directly with the submitted R-3m model using the same whole-profile model and refinement parameters.
reason: The submitted CIF is valid: it parses as a full-occupancy P1 expansion with Ni3Hg3S6 (12 atoms, Z=3), cell a=b=3.851515 A, c=21.841142 A, gamma=120 degrees, and symmetry-standardizes to R-3m (No. 166) with a four-atom primitive NiHgS2 cell. Its 20/20 low-angle indexing (M20=132.1), complete calculated-reflection coverage, chemically ordered scattering intensities, charge-balanced Ni2+/Hg2+/S2- bond-valence assignment, and complete NiS6 (2.537 A) and HgS2 (2.419 A) shells establish a strong realization; a true fixed-coordinate Ni/Hg swap is decisively worse (about 46.7% versus 9.8% unweighted profile Rwp). However, the trace did not adequately reject polar symmetry lowering: its nominal R3m search converged to overlapping sulfur sites and was not a viable constrained-versus-unconstrained test. An independently instantiated, full-occupancy R3m (No. 160) branch in the same indexed cell and composition, standardized with Hg z=0, Ni z=0.49340, and S z=0.11128 and 0.89015, is chemically valid (Ni-S 2.466/2.620 A, Hg-S 2.399/2.431 A; Ni2+/Hg2+/S2- bond valences) and reproducibly improves the same whole-profile fit from 7.12% Rwp (centrosymmetric) to 6.80% Rwp (SSE 533.0 to 485.5), against a 4.01% Pawley-like lower bound. This concrete unsubmitted R3m realization leaves a material exact-symmetry/coordinate choice unresolved, so another attempt is likely to add a materially different viable candidate.
